append.text: **Ps 12:1–3: four *Até quando*** — *Úsquequo* ×3 and 12:2 *Quámdiu*, merged (the Latin's anaphora is the psalm's shape; the stylist praised the repeated *Até quando*; *Por quanto tempo* for *quámdiu* is option 2). *quámdiu* elsewhere is "as long as" (103:33 *quámdiu sum*, 145:2a *quámdiu fúero*) and decides there.

Ps 12:2 *Até quando hei de pôr conselhos na minha alma* — the stylist's *hei de pôr* (a deliberative future) for draft 1's *porei*; the blind reader heard advice kept first, deliberation second — the Latin's range; *planos* (MS1932 *projectos*) is an option.

Ps 12:2 *e dor no meu coração durante o dia* — second object of *hei de pôr* (the Latin's asyndeton *ponam consília …, dolórem …*); *e* supplied after the blind reader heard draft 1's bare *dor* as "while there is sorrow".

**Ps 12:1 *avértis fáciem tuam a me* → *desviais de mim a vossa face*** (the formula; 9 lines with *fáciem tuam a*: 26:9, 29:8, 50:11, 68:18, 87:15, 101:3, 142:7b …; 9:32 *desviou a sua face* in Ps 9 agrees). *Desviar* keeps *avértere* one verb with or without a dative; the Latinist passed it twice.

**Ps 12:3 the imperative *réspice* → bare *olhai*** (*olhai, e escutai-me, Senhor, meu Deus*): the Latin has no object, and *me* hangs on both verbs as the Latin's does; *olhai para mim* is option 2; passed by the Latinist twice. 83:10 still decides locally.
Ps 12:5b *Os que me atribulam* — listed as unknown by both blind readings of Ps 12; kept.

Ps 12:5b *exultarão*, 12:6b *O meu coração exultará na vossa salvação* (9:16a *Exultarei na vossa salvação* in Ps 9 agrees); the second blind reading listed *exultarão* and *exultará* as unknown; kept.
Ps 12:6b: the 7:18b colon copied word for word, as the formula row asked; passed by the Latinist twice, soft length flag +5 accepted as in Ps 7.

terms: | in finem | para sempre | open | Ps 12:1 *me esquecereis para sempre?* (Ps 9 proposed it for 9:7a, 9:19, 9:32; followed). 22 lines have *finem* (grep), the adverbial *in finem* in most: 43:23, 51:7, 67:17b, 73:1, 73:3, 73:10, 73:11, 73:19, 76:9, 78:5, 88:47 … — with *úsquequo* three times (12:1, 78:5, 88:47), where "how long … for ever?" is the Latin's own. **Collides with D23 *in ætérnum* → para sempre** where both occur near each other (48:9 has both in one colon: *in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem*) — 48:9 must decide locally; *até o fim* is the option. The blind reader heard 12:1 as "forgotten me for good?" |

| oblivísci, *obliviscéris* (12:1) | esquecer (*me esquecereis*) | open | Ps 12:1 — **the future, by the accent**: *obliviscéris* (long ē) against the present 43:24 *oblivísceris* (Greek ἐπιλήσῃ, future). **The Latinist (Ps 12 draft 2, MAJOR) read a present and asked for *me esqueceis*; refused** — he passed the same words on draft 1. The accent in the psalter text is the evidence to cite whenever a 3rd-conjugation *-eris* comes up |

| obdormíre | adormecer (*para que eu nunca adormeça na morte*) | open | Ps 12:4b; 43:23 *quare obdórmis, Dómine?* (of God) is the only other (grep) and should follow (*por que adormeceis*); the blind reader heard "so that I do not die" first; *dormir* is *dormíre*'s (3:6, 4:9) |

| movéri (*motus fúero*, *movébor*) | ser abalado (*se eu for abalado*) | open | Ps 12:5b; *Non movébor* 9:27 (Ps 9 agent: *Não serei abalado*, agreeing), 29:7, 61:3; 93:18 *Motus est pes meus*. Heard as shaken in spirit first, defeated second — the Latin's range. *vacilar*, *cair* are options |

| præválere (advérsus) | prevalecer (contra) (*Prevaleci contra ele*) | open | Ps 12:4b(5a); 51:9 *et præváluit in vanitáte sua*, 64:4 *Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos* (grep, 3 lines); the Latin's own descendant |
| per diem | durante o dia | open | Ps 12:2; heard as "all day long" first; *cada dia* (MS1932), *o dia todo* are options; *tota die* (37:7 …) is another phrase and should keep *o dia todo* |

| bona tríbuere | dar coisas boas (*que me deu coisas boas*) | open | Ps 12:6b; draft 1 *que me concedeu bens* was heard by the blind reader as property and called administrative by the stylist, whose wording this is; the Greek has τῷ εὐεργετήσαντί με. *tríbuere* and *dare* never meet in a verse, so *dar* is free; 15:7 *qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum* can read *que me deu entendimento* |
formulas: | *Úsquequo, Dómine, … in finem?* (12:1 *obliviscéris me in finem*; 78:5 *irascéris in finem*; 88:47 *avértis in finem*) | *Até quando, Senhor, … para sempre?* | open — Ps 12 (*Até quando, Senhor, me esquecereis para sempre?*); 78:5 and 88:47 should follow |
